title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 60
paragraphs: Having thus recovered the tyranny in the manner described, Peisistratus, in accordance with the agreement he had made with Megacles, married the daughter of Megacles. But as he already had young sons, and as the descendants of Alcmaeon were said to be under a curse, he did not wish children to be born to him from his newly married wife, and so had intercourse with her in an unaccustomed manner. At first the woman kept this secret, but afterwards she told her mother—whether in answer to her inquiry or not I cannot say—and the mother told her husband Megacles. He then was deeply indignant at being dishonored by Peisistratus, and in his anger immediately moved to compose his quarrel with the men of his faction. When Peisistratus heard what was being done against him, he departed entirely from the land and came to Eretria, where he took counsel together with his sons. When the advice of Hippias prevailed—that they should try to win back the tyranny—they began to gather gifts of money from those states that owed them obligations for favors received. Many contributed great sums, but the Thebans surpassed the rest in the giving of money. Then, not to make the story long, time passed and at last everything was prepared for their return. For certain Argives came as mercenaries from the Peloponnesus, and a man of Naxos called Lygdamis had come to them of his own accord, showing very great zeal in providing both money and men.
